chunks: Ali, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them) who said:

A man complained to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) of pain in his chest, so he (peace be upon him and his family) said: Seek healing through the Quran, for indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, says:
'and a healing for what is in the chests' [Quran 10:57].

key_terms.اسْتَشْفِ: Seek healing — imperative form of istishfa', seeking cure through a means
key_terms.الصُّدُور: The chests/breasts — in classical Arabic thought, the seat of the heart, emotions, and spiritual states
key_terms.شِفَاءٌ: Healing, cure — the Quran is described as a shifa' (healing) for what is in the chests

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about seeking healing through the Quran?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates through his forefathers that a man came to the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) complaining of chest pain. The Prophet directed him to seek healing through the Quran, citing Quran 10:57 which describes the Quran as 'a healing for what is in the chests.' This hadith establishes the Quran as a source of spiritual and physical healing (ruqya), a practice deeply rooted in early Islamic tradition where Quranic recitation was understood as a remedy for ailments of both body and soul.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A man complained to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> of pain in his chest, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Seek healing with the Quran, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Saying
[10:57] and a Healing for what is in the chests’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Once a man complained to the Holy Prophet for having pain in his chest and he (a.s.) said, ‘Seek a cure from the Holy Quran; Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, says,
“It is a cure for that which is in the chest (the heart).”’
